status: The schema is defined and the client code ships. Nothing is being collected on the live site, because no endpoint is configured.
principles: No cookies, no local storage, no device identifiers, no IP address stored.
Five named events, and nothing else. The browser refuses to send an event outside the allowlist.
A click is not an order. This measures interest, not revenue.
If the endpoint is unset, the code fails open and sends nothing — the page must never depend on the network.
Outbound links are never routed through a redirect, because Program Policies 6(v) treats a Redirecting Link as cloaking and 6(w) bars a shortener that obscures the Amazon destination.

events.name: page_view
events.fires: Once per page load, after the page is interactive.

events.name: category_view
events.fires: When a category or cluster page is viewed.

events.name: product_view
events.fires: When a product page is viewed.

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires: On click of an Amazon link, before the browser follows it.

events.name: guide_read_75
events.fires: Once per guide, when the reader has scrolled past 75% of the article.

not_collected: Amazon order, commission or customer data of any kind

endpoint_contract.response: 204 on accept, 400 on an unknown event or an unexpected property

reference_implementations: tools/analytics-endpoint/server.py and worker.js in the repository root
collector.storage: One append-only JSONL file per day, aggregate counts only; no identifier that could re-link a visitor across days.
collector.deployment: GitHub Pages cannot run any of these. The endpoint must be deployed elsewhere and its URL set in the build configuration before a single event is sent.
